@graph.description: Compare recruitment agencies and in-house hiring across cost, control, sourcing and scalability for Indian employers. A balanced EarlyJobs guide—no fake benchmarks.

mainEntity.name: Is an agency cheaper than in-house recruitment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Neither model is cheaper by default. In-house teams carry payroll, tools and management overhead; agencies often charge placement fees or project fees tied to scope. Compare your hiring mix, volume and internal capacity—not headline rates alone.

mainEntity.name: Can companies use both recruitment models?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many Indian employers keep core roles in-house and use agencies for spikes, niche skills or new locations. A hybrid model works when responsibilities, SLAs and commercial terms are documented before sourcing begins.

mainEntity.name: Who makes the final hiring decision?

acceptedAnswer.text: The employer ordinarily retains final selection authority unless a different lawful arrangement is explicitly agreed. Agencies may shortlist and coordinate, but culture fit, compensation approval and offer release typically stay internal.

mainEntity.name: When should a company consider an agency?

acceptedAnswer.text: Consider an agency when internal TA lacks bandwidth, specialist networks or geographic reach for a hiring burst. Agencies add sourcing capacity and flexibility, scoped by agreed services and fees—not guaranteed headcount outcomes.
